note: پیغام centrally means message/news/communication. 'Advice' can occur contextually but should not be the leading gloss.
Common literary/poetic mind/heart/soul reading omitted while rare unit leads.
proposed_english: mind; heart; soul; will; maund (unit of mass) (context-dependent)

note: شب means night/evening in Urdu/Persian-derived vocabulary. 'Alum' is unrelated source contamination.
فرض centrally means duty/obligation and also an obligatory religious act/prayer; it can mean assumption/supposition in technical contexts. Adjective POS is unnecessary.
proposed_english: duty; obligation; obligatory religious act/prayer; assumption/supposition

note: مملکت centrally means state/country/kingdom/realm. 'Grandeur, magnificence' is unrelated/noisy and the modern political sense 'state' is missing.
Besides Arabic-derived لا 'not', the same Urdu spelling is the stem/imperative form of لانا 'to bring'; this is a common form-level homograph.
proposed_english: not; bring!/bring (stem or imperative of لانا, context-dependent)

note: اکبر is an Arabic comparative/superlative adjective meaning greater/greatest and a common proper name Akbar. 'Closed-class' is incorrect.
صفائی centrally means cleanliness/cleaning/hygiene and can mean explanation/defense/exoneration in legal or argumentative contexts. 'Truthfulness' is not a core meaning.
تیسری is the feminine form of تیسرا 'third' and functions as an adjective/determiner, not an unspecified closed-class item.
حافظ means guardian/protector/keeper and especially a person who has memorized the Qur'an; it is also a name/title. 'Governor' is not an appropriate core gloss.
proposed_english: guardian; protector; keeper; person who has memorized the Qur'an; Hafiz (name/title)

note: کپڑے is an inflected/plural form of کپڑا and must explicitly give clothes/clothing/cloth rather than only inflection labels.
ریاض in Urdu is most commonly a male name Riaz/Riyaz and the Arabic place name Riyadh; etymologically it means gardens. 'Toil; practice; training' is confusion with ریاضت.
ذات means self/being/essence and very commonly caste/community background in South Asian usage. The caste sense is missing.
عطا means giving/grant/gift/bestowal and appears in عطا کرنا 'to grant/bestow'. 'Giving' alone is too narrow.
بلا is a homograph: bi-lā functions as without/without any, while balā means calamity/disaster/affliction. Noun-only POS misses the prepositional use.
proposed_english: without; calamity; disaster; affliction (depending on vocalization/context)

note: نواب is the historical title nawab, a Muslim noble/ruler/governor. 'A rich Mughal ruler' is overly narrow and inaccurate as a general definition.
